title: Dinosaurs for Kids! 5 Dino Surprises with Dash
intro: Hi, friends! I'm Dash, your little dino buddy, and welcome to Dino World Kids!
Today we're going way back in time to meet five amazing dinosaur friends.
Can you count them with me? One, two, three, four, five!
Ready? Let's stomp, stomp, stomp back in time!

lines: Here's our first friend. Here's a clue: it was huge, but it had super tiny arms! Can you guess?
T. rex was one of the biggest dinosaurs that ever walked on land.
Scientists think it had a super strong nose for smelling things far away.
Can you sniff, sniff, sniff like T. rex?
Can you guess? Could T. rex reach its mouth with its arms?
No! Its arms were too short. They were tiny!
Let's say it together: T. REX!
T. rex lived about 66 million years ago.
Who's next? Here's a clue: it had three horns and a big frill on its head! Can you guess?
It had a big bony frill around its neck, like a giant collar.
Can you make three horns with your fingers?
Can you guess what Triceratops liked to eat?
Plants! Triceratops munched on leafy plants all day.
Triceratops lived at the same time as T. rex.
Who's next? Here's a clue: it had big plates on its back and a spiky tail! Can you guess?
Stegosaurus had big plates on its back, in two rows.
Scientists think the plates helped it show off, or warm up in the sun.
Can you make a spiky back? Stretch up tall!
Can you guess what its spiky tail is called?
A thagomizer! What a funny word!
Stegosaurus lived long, long before T. rex. They never met!
Who's next? Here's a clue: it had a super long neck and it was very, very tall! Can you guess?
Brachiosaurus was taller than a house!
Its front legs were longer than its back legs, like a giraffe.
Can you stretch up high, high, high?
Can you guess why it needed such a long neck?
To reach the leaves at the very top of the trees! Munch, munch!
Who's last? Here's a clue: it flew in the sky with giant wings! Can you guess?
Pteranodon had wings wider than a car!
It soared high above the sea.
Can you flap your arms like big wings? Flap, flap!
Can you guess? Was Pteranodon a dinosaur?
No! It was a flying reptile called a pterosaur. A dinosaur cousin!
Its name means toothless wing, because it had no teeth.

recap: What a dino adventure! Let's remember.
Stegosaurus had a spiky tail called a thagomizer.
Brachiosaurus was taller than a house.
And Pteranodon was a flying reptile, not a dinosaur!
outro: Here's a secret: birds are living dinosaurs! So say hi to the birds outside. Be kind to every animal.
Bye, friends! See you in Dino World!
